newsitem.title: NIGERIA: World Bank ends failed Nigeria roads project.
newsitem.headline: World Bank ends failed Nigeria roads project.

text.p: The World Bank on Tuesday said it had closed a $250 million loan to revamp Nigeria's roads, saying the project had failed in the face of mismanagement and political and economic instability.

In a statement released in the Nigerian capital, the bank said only $120 million of the original loan amount of $250 million, approved in June 1988, had been spent, despite extensions of the original closing date of June 1993.
It said the main reasons for the failure of the project were the political and macroeconomic instability in Nigeria during the project's implementation.
Flagged at the outset as a project to rehabilitate 1,500 km (900 miles) of roads and build 17 bridges, the result was about 500 km (300 miles) of road works and seven bridges completed.
Political and economic crisis have gripped Africa's most populous nation since the annulment of 1993 elections by a military government.

While current military ruler General Sani Abacha won World Bank praise for tough anti-inflation policies, his clique of generals has not grasped the nettle of privatising state enterprises or abolishing dual exchange rates and subsidies.
The cancelled road project suffered from frequent changes in key government personnel, long delays in decision making, delays in payments to contractors and a lack of bitumen, the bank said.
"The lesson learnt from this project is that fundamental restructuring as to how roads are managed in Nigeria is required," the statement said.
